title: Cultivating a Three-dimensional Reconstructed Human Epidermis at a Large Scale
protocol: Review national and international ethical considerations related to human tissues or cells.
Adhere to conditions for the use of human tissues or cells before planning research activities.
Carry out all steps in aseptic conditions.
Follow Biosafety Level 2 practices for cultivating RhEs.
Take necessary safety precautions when handling chemicals/reagents.
Prepare basal medium by mixing Keratinocyte growth medium with 1% [v/v] HKGS and 1% [v/v] antibiotic-antimycotic.
Prepare submerged medium by mixing Keratinocyte growth medium with 1% [v/v] HKGS, 1% [v/v] antibiotic-antimycotic, and adding 1.5 mM Ca2+.
Prepare the basal medium.
Supplement the bottle of 500 mL of keratinocyte growth medium with 5 mL of human keratinocyte growth supplements (HKGS).
Add 5 mL of 100x antibiotic-antimycotic solution containing 10,000 units/mL of penicillin, 10,000 µg/mL of streptomycin, and 25 µg/mL of amphotericin B.
Prepare the submerged medium.
Supplement the bottle of 500 mL of keratinocyte growth medium with 5 mL of HKGS.
Add 5 mL of 100x antibiotic-antimycotic solution.
Add 5 mL of a 0.144 M CaCl2 stock solution to reach a final concentration of 1.5 mM Ca2+.
Supplement one bottle of 500 mL of keratinocyte growth medium with 5 mL of HKGS.
Add 5 mL of 100x antibiotic-antimycotic solution.
Add 5 mL of a 0.144 M CaCl2 stock solution to reach a final concentration of 1.5 mM Ca2+.
Add 1 mL of a 25 mg/mL ascorbic acid stock solution to reach a final concentration of 50 µg/mL ascorbic acid.
Add 50 μL of a 100 µg/mL KGF in 1% [w/v] bovine serum albumin in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) stock solution to reach a final concentration of 10 ng/mL KGF.
Thaw a vial containing 1 x 10^6 cryopreserved NHEKs in a water bath at 37°C until only a small sliver of ice remains.
Wipe the vial with a 70% ethanol solution before transferring it into the laminar hood.
Resuspend cells carefully by pipetting up and down 2-3 times.
Transfer cell suspension into two T75 flasks containing a total of 15 mL of pre-warmed thawing medium, resulting in a seeding density of 6.7 x 10^4 cells/cm².
Place the flasks into the cell culture incubator (37°C, 5% CO₂, and 95% RH).
After approximately 24 hours, replace the thawing medium with basal medium to remove DMSO from the keratinocyte freezing solution.
Refresh the basal medium every two days.
After 4-6 days of cultivation, prepare cells for seeding in inserts when they reach around 80% confluence.
Pre-fill 24-well plates with 1.5 mL of submerged medium using a dispenser pipette.
Remove the basal medium from T75 flasks used for culturing NHEKs.
Rinse the cells by adding 5 mL of pre-warmed PBS to each T75 flask.
Remove PBS from the flasks.
Add 2-3 mL of pre-warmed 0.05% [v/v] trypsin/ethylene diamine tetra acetic acid (EDTA) to each T75 flask.
Place the flasks for 4 minutes in the cell culture incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% RH.
Check whether the cells detach using a microscope at 10x magnification.
Rap the flask against the palm of the hand to help the cells release from the surface of the flask.
Once all the cells are detached, add an equal volume (i.e., 2-3 mL) of pre-warmed trypsin inhibitor to each T75 flask.
Transfer the cell suspension from the flasks to a centrifuge tube.
Rinse the flasks with 5 mL of pre-warmed PBS and transfer it to the centrifuge tube containing the cell suspension.
Check the number of residual cells in the flasks under the microscope.
Centrifuge the harvested cells at 400 x g for 5 min.
Carefully discard most of the supernatant, leaving approximately 100-200 μL in the tube.
Gently resuspend the pellet of cells in a low volume of submerged medium.
Pipette up and down 5-10 times to ensure a uniform cell suspension.
Dilute 0.4% [v/v] trypan blue stain and the cell suspension in a 1:1 ratio by adding 10 μL of 0.4% [v/v] trypan blue stain to 10 μL of cell suspension.
Add 10 μL of the solution to a counting slide.
Measure the cell count immediately after mixing the cell suspension with trypan blue.
Hang the 24 cell culture inserts in the highest position of the recommended carrier plate.
Transfer the carrier plate to the 24-well plate pre-filled with submerged medium.
Add the determined volume V4 of the cell suspension to each insert using reverse pipetting technique.
Incubate the 24-well plates for 10-15 min at room temperature, without moving the plates during this time.
Transfer the plates to the cell culture incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% RH).
Maintain the cells in submerged conditions for three days.
Avoid stacking plates in the incubator after seeding to ensure uniform heat distribution for each insert.
Incubate cells for three days at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% RH.
Remove submerged medium from the apical compartment using an aspiration system and a glass Pasteur pipette.
Alternatively, remove submerged medium with a manual micropipette.
Fill new 24-well plates with 1.5 mL of fresh pre-warmed ALI medium.
Transfer carrier plates with culture inserts to the new multi-well plates containing ALI medium.
Incubate the multi-well plates at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% RH.
Refresh ALI medium every 2-3 days for 14 days by preparing a new plate with fresh pre-warmed ALI medium.
Transfer carrier plates to the newly prepared plate containing ALI medium.
Maintain RhEs protected from potential contamination during reconstitution by not removing the lid covering the carrier plate.
Perform an air-liquid interface (ALI) step for the development of a stratified epidermal model, allowing terminal differentiation of keratinocytes.
Check for medium droplets on tissue surface coming from the basolateral compartment to identify any 'leaky tissues'.
Gently remove the medium from the culture insert if leakage occurs at ALI day 3 without touching the surface of the tissue.
Discard leaking tissues if the leakage persists, indicating no correct barrier formation in the RhE model.
Expose the reconstituted tissues to various stressors or chemical compounds for inducing oxidative stress or inflammation.
Maintain tissues in submerged medium starting from ALI D14 during exposure/treatment.

Start the exposure/treatment earlier in the ALI cultivation process if tissues are expected to be exposed for a long period (i.e., 48-72 hours) to avoid thinning of viable layers and thickening of the SC.
Incubate tissues in ALI medium to keep stimulating cell proliferation during prolonged exposure periods.
Collect tissues at the timepoint of interest for histological analysis.
Collect cell culture medium at the timepoint of interest for viability assays.
Extract proteins and RNA from collected tissues at the timepoint of interest.
Perform enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) using collected cell culture medium.
